requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
I found no gap. Each obligation of `requirements.authoring.invocation` is carried out by code reachable from the `{impl}` items, and each has a test.

**Command form and alias.** The `Command::Author` variant in `src/main.rs#enum[Command]` defines these things:
- the `subject` argument and the `--config`, `--stdout` and `-v/--verbose` options;
- `--missing` and `--force`, which conflict with each other, and `--missing`, which conflicts with `--stdout`;
- the `author-evidence` alias.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` and the batch test in `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` assert that conflicting flags are rejected. Several tests run `author-evidence`, including `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free`, `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` and the batch test. `--config mock` is exercised with a single subject in `tests/authoring_cli.rs`, for example in `fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]`.

**Author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example, under refresh.**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[AuthoringSubject]/fn[parse]` and `fn[author_evidence_with_options]` take the subject. They apply `--force`, and `--stdout` implies it. Under `--missing` they call `batch::subject_is_current` and return `None` when the record is current.
- `fn[configured_assessment]` and `fn[configured_record]` carry out the assessment and write the file.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare]` rejects a name that is not an existing requirement or named example ("no matching requirement or named example").
- The unknown-subject case is tested by `author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets`.
- The refresh behavior is tested by `missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject`. That test covers keeping current records without configuration, `--force` reassessing, `--stdout` implying `--force`, and the "1 skipped as current" report.

**Report on completion: subject, backend, model, evidence destination, usage path.**
- `struct[AuthoringOutcome]` carries these fields.
- `fn[main]` prints `"{subject}: {backend} / {model}; policy …"`, then `Evidence: …`, then `Usage: …`.
- `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` asserts the stdout starts with `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL`, that the `Evidence:` path ends in `evidence/SUBJECT.json` and resolves to the project's evidence file, and that `Usage:` appears.

**Evidence destination is the file path by default and stdout under `--stdout`.**
- `enum[EvidenceOutput]` and `fn[configured_assessment]` set `evidence_path` to `Some(path)` for a file and `None` for stdout.
- `fn[main]` prints `Evidence: stdout` in the stdout case.
- Both cases are tested. The default case is covered in `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free`. The stdout case is covered in `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files`, which asserts `Evidence: stdout`.

**Stdout mode sends the completion report and diagnostics to stderr.**
- In `fn[main]`, the report and the false-judgment diagnostics (the "false" line and, with `--verbose`, the rationale) use `eprintln!` in stdout mode. Coverage warnings are skipped there.
- `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` parses all of stdout as JSON. It asserts that subject, backend, model, `Evidence: stdout` and the usage path are on stderr, and that the false/FIXME diagnostics and the verbose rationale also appear on stderr.

No unspecified behavior or untested obligation stands out, and there are no `{fixme}` references.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
